prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_D:
Summary of proposals (2001)

Health
- Cut waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied health professionals; add 10,000 hospital beds.
- Improve retention with average £1,000 pay rises for lowest-paid NHS staff; commission on NHS pay and conditions.
- Free personal care for elderly/long-term patients; restore free dental and eye checks; double investment in scanners; £500m to guarantee NHS dentistry access.
- Create a Pharmaceutical Agency to end “postcode lottery,” use NHS purchasing power, and move toward scrapping prescription charges.
- Patient Care Guarantees; stronger local accountability; independent advocacy (incl. Children’s Rights Commissioner); no-fault compensation; end mixed wards; ban age discrimination in care.

Education, skills and work
- Primary classes averaged at 25; recruit 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants (25,000 in Key Stage 1); two paid prep hours weekly for primary teachers; paid training salary for trainees; reduce bureaucracy and testing at age 7.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorer students; raise loan repayment threshold; oppose top-up fees; improve HE staff pay.
- Adult entitlement to funded tuition (to Level 2; to Level 3 for 16–24s); merge skills funders into a Learning Council; SME training incentives; paid study leave for 16–24s; replace New Deal with a Flexible Guarantee via a combined Benefits and Jobs Agency.

Law, order and justice
- 6,000 additional police officers; 2,000 part-time retained community officers; Community Safety Force for low-level disorder.
- Independent police complaints system; community-focused partnerships; cooperation with Europol.
- Shift from costly prison expansion to effective alternatives; full working day, skills and rehabilitation in prisons; reduce reoffending.
- Stronger victims’ rights (impact statements, information); tackle hate crimes; retain jury trial; end most mandatory sentencing; expand restorative and youth justice reforms.

Transport
- Free off-peak local bus travel for pensioners and disabled people; aim half-price fares for under-19s in education.
- Abolish Vehicle Excise Duty for the cleanest vehicles; higher VED for most polluting; no real-terms rise in fuel duty next Parliament.
- Enable local funding tools (bonds, congestion charging, parking levies); create a Sustainable Transport Authority; stronger public control of rail investment and safety; restructure rail infrastructure into a not-for-profit public-interest model; rural transport fund; priority to road maintenance and safety; not-for-profit air traffic control; tighter night flight limits.

Pensions, wages and benefits
- Increase basic state pension (£5/week single; more for over-75s/80s; proportional rises for couples); scrap savings penalty; establish an Independent Pensions Authority; relax annuity rules; develop personal second pensions and extend basic entitlement over time.
- Annual review of the minimum wage; single full rate from age 16.
- Extra £200 for children in families on long-term income support; replace the Child Support Agency with family courts.
- Improve support for disabled people (incl. winter fuel payments for the severely disabled); simplify housing benefit; fairer utility tariffs; better cold weather payments; reduce tax on the lowest paid over time.

Culture, media and sport
- Embed arts in schools; restore free instrumental tuition funding; lower VAT on renovation (and apply low rate to new build); universal free internet access in libraries.
- Create OFCOM; redefine public service broadcasting; reform BBC governance; tighter cross-media ownership; community sports plans.

Business, consumers and environment
- Scrap unnecessary regulations; small business rates allowance; stronger competition law; improved consumer and bank protections; Post Office universal service.
- Replace the Climate Change Levy with a carbon tax; emissions trading; at least 10% renewable energy by 2010 rising annually; phase out nuclear as stations retire; expand research funding; ethical corporate reporting.

Political and civil rights
- Referendum on AV+ for Westminster; STV for local/European elections; voting and candidacy from 16; elected Senate to replace the Lords; stronger parliamentary scrutiny; local income tax.
- Stronger Freedom of Information; Equality Act and Equality Commission; civil partnership registration; judicial oversight of surveillance; no ID cards.
- Fairer, faster asylum system; end vouchers; improve support and local compensation.

Communities, rural and housing
- National doorstep recycling (60% in 10 years); flood defence task force; GM crop moratorium until 2004; marine protected areas.
- One-stop regeneration grants; brownfield-first with planning and VAT reform; protect green spaces; require planning for mobile masts.
- Reform CAP/CFP toward sustainability and local co-management; support tenant and organic farming; create a Ministry for Rural Affairs; protect village services; measures on affordability, empty homes, and leasehold rights; option for site value rating.

Europe, defence and international
- EU constitutional settlement clarifying powers; subsidiarity and transparency; accountable Commission/Council; enlargement; single Parliament seat in Brussels.
- Maintain defence spending; flexible, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing disarmament; oppose national missile defence; moratorium on depleted uranium.
- End subsidies for arms exports; strengthen UN (incl. rapid reaction/disaster capacity, ICC); fairer WTO rules with environmental integration; aid to 0.7% GNI, untied and focused on gender, health (HIV/AIDS), and education; stronger climate commitments (e.g., CO2 −20% by 2010).

Economy and tax
- Enhance Bank of England independence (non-renewable MPC terms, transparent appointments).
- Enable euro entry via referendum at a competitive rate.
- Allow devolved/regional/local borrowing for investment.
- Fund priorities through 1p on income tax for education; 50% top rate above £100k for pensions and NHS; CGT simplification; Citizen’s Tax Contract; annual independent fiscal assessment; green tax reform matched by cuts elsewhere; reduce tax burden on lowest incomes over time.

TEXT_C:
Summary of proposals and positions (ideology removed)

- European Union and currency
  - Withdraw from the EU; repeal the European Communities Act 1972.
  - Negotiate trade agreements with European states and others; keep the pound permanently.
  - Maintain Bank of England interest-rate independence.

- Economy, trade, and regulation
  - Pursue global free trade, deepen ties with Commonwealth and North America.
  - Large-scale deregulation, prioritising small and medium-sized enterprises; review metrication and abattoir rules.
  - Simplify and reduce taxes: raise the income tax threshold to remove ~1 million low earners from tax, reform inheritance and capital gains taxes, consider replacing VAT with a retail sales tax after EU exit.
  - Oppose tax harmonisation.

- Independence Dividend (estimated ~£20bn annually)
  - Savings from ending EU budget contributions and gains from deregulation and growth.
  - Planned allocations include: agriculture (£2bn), regional support (£1bn), state pension uplift (£2.8bn), elderly care (£0.5bn), restoring frozen expat pensions (£0.3bn), tax changes (£2.7bn total), NHS (£2bn) plus nursing pay (£0.5bn), 30,000 more teachers (£1.2bn), 25,000 more police (£0.8bn), fuel duty cut (9p/litre; ~£3.7bn), defence (£2.5bn).

- Health and social care
  - Increase NHS funding; restore clearer hospital management roles (e.g., matron-style leadership), reduce bureaucracy, focus on infection control and patient care.
  - Improve nurse pay and retention; rebalance training toward practical competence; recruit internationally where needed.
  - Review and simplify social services; reduce bureaucracy and focus on practical outcomes.

- Welfare and pensions
  - Simplify benefits to reduce fraud and administration; ensure work always pays.
  - Consider basic income-style support for specific groups to aid re-entry to work.
  - Raise state pension by £5/week; increase elderly care funding; restore full pensions to affected expatriates.
  - Explore partial diversion of National Insurance into personal pension funds (grandfathering existing pensioners).

- Education
  - Allow selection/streaming; target class sizes under 25; hire more teachers; elevate technical/vocational routes; consider vouchers; encourage specialist and single-sex or faith options where desired.
  - Reform teacher training toward proven methods; address discipline and attainment gaps.
  - Protect school sports and halt sale of playing fields.
  - Support independent funding models for higher education; encourage private universities with scholarships; treat overseas students equally by origin.

- Transport and environment
  - Integrated transport; case-by-case approach to ownership/privatisation; oppose part-sale of London Underground.
  - Reduce fuel duty; fund bypasses, route upgrades, maintenance, cycle lanes; adjust vehicle tax by emissions.
  - Decentralise environmental enforcement to local authorities; strengthen monitoring of pollution-related health impacts.
  - Strong GMO labelling and protections; encourage renewables (biofuels, wave, wind, solar, hydrogen).

- Home affairs, justice, and rights
  - Protect jury trial and common-law safeguards; oppose EU-wide legal and policing integration.
  - Repeal and reenact the Human Rights Act to align with domestic legal tradition.
  - Increase police numbers; prioritise visible, community-linked policing; use rehabilitation and non-custodial sentences for non-violent offences; “life means life” for the most serious crimes.

- Immigration and asylum
  - Skills-based immigration model; equalise treatment for family reunification compared with non-EU countries.
  - Speed up asylum processing with reception centres; tighten monitoring; prioritise first safe country principles; seek reform of the 1951 Refugee Convention.

- Agriculture and fisheries
  - Replace CAP with national policy; introduce voluntary Land Management Contracts paying for agreed environmental and land-use outcomes; support organics and higher welfare; assist young farmers; enable diversification and farmers’ markets.
  - Amend right-to-roam to reflect local conditions.
  - Exit the Common Fisheries Policy; exclusive national control up to 200 miles under international law; create recovery zones and ban damaging methods; allow access via bilateral agreements.

- Defence and foreign affairs
  - Increase defence spending on personnel and equipment; prioritise NATO; leave EU defence structures.
  - Pursue cost-effective procurement, including from the US.
  - Refocus aid toward communities, with governance and freedom conditions.

- Constitution and governance
  - Enact a UK Bill of Rights preventing transfer of sovereignty without consent.
  - Strengthen Parliament over the executive; empower select committees; review quangos.
  - Oppose regionalisation; consider a further Welsh referendum; address West Lothian question; restore county-based local government; enable citizen-initiated local referenda with an impartial referendum commission.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_D" | "TEXT_C"
}
